issues.description: The problem statement contains conflicting signatures for the milk operation: the UML and other parts specify Milkable.messageOnMilk() with no parameters, but the Part 2 textual description asks for messageOnMilk(double milkVolume). The template/solution code and example usage use the no-argument version. This inconsistency can confuse students about which method signature to implement and may lead to compilation/test failures if they follow the erroneous textual description.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the problem statement consistent: either (A) require messageOnMilk() with no parameters everywhere (update the Part 2 textual description to remove the double parameter and volume formatting), or (B) change the UML, template, and solution to use messageOnMilk(double milkVolume) and update all usages accordingly. Prefer option (A) to match the provided template and solution unless explicit milk volume tracking is intended.

issues.description: The problem statement (text) specifies a Milkable method signature messageOnMilk(double milkVolume) (introducing the parameter identifier 'milkVolume'), but the UML in the problem statement and all code artifacts (template usage in Main.java and the solution's Milkable interface and implementations) define and use messageOnMilk() with no parameter. This mismatch in the method signature / parameter identifier can confuse students about the exact method they must implement and which parameter name (milkVolume) is expected.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the specification consistent across all artifacts. Either (A) change the problem statement text to require messageOnMilk() with no parameters (removing the 'double milkVolume' mention), or (B) modify the interface and implementations to declare messageOnMilk(double milkVolume) and update all call sites (e.g., Main.java and tests) and implementations (Seal, Goat) to accept the parameter and include it in the returned string (e.g., "Seal [name] is milked (volume: [milkVolume]L)").
